about: Held-out prospect questions, in the same format as questions.json. Neo's rules are never tuned against these: they check that a score on questions.json reflects the job rather than the test. Run them at release time with --set holdout. All questions are synthetic.

questions.q: Do you come to the office? We're in Brooklyn.
questions.expect: Yes, on-site work is within about 30 miles of Queens, which Brooklyn is; otherwise remote; no promise of a date.

questions.q: Can you work during the day on a Tuesday?
questions.expect: Gives the published hours (weekends 8am to 8pm, weekday evenings 6pm to 9pm Eastern) so a weekday daytime slot isn't the usual; points to the booking calendar or Pradeep.

questions.q: I don't like phone calls. Can I get started some other way?
questions.expect: Yes: a free 1NEON account where they write down what they need and ask for an assessment, or email.
Yes: bank transfer or card online, or check, Zelle, or wire, with no surcharge; invoices come through 1NEON, due within 15 days.

questions.q: If you set things up, who owns the accounts afterwards?
questions.expect: The business keeps its accounts and data, with a clean way out; neon1 uses only the access needed and removes it when done.

questions.q: Do you need money up front?
questions.expect: A project usually starts with a deposit and the rest is billed at handover; each project is priced in a proposal you can say no to.

questions.q: Roughly what would it cost to get our invoices out of Word and into something automatic?
questions.expect: Gives the published range that fits (a workflow project, $1,000 to $3,000, or a small fix if it is narrow) as a guide, not a quote; the proposal gives the exact figure.

questions.q: Our Shopify stock never matches what's on the shelf. Is that something you fix?
questions.expect: General information on why counts drift (sales in more than one place, manual updates) and that connecting the flow is neon1's workflow work; asks what tools they use or offers the call; no promise.

questions.q: Can Google Forms feed straight into a Google Sheet?
questions.expect: Yes, generally: Google Forms can send responses to a linked Sheet; framed as general information; may mention neon1 can connect the steps after it.

questions.q: Our security cameras record but never send alerts. Can you sort that out?
questions.expect: Networks and devices work covers cameras that don't alert; typical length for one office is 1 to 2 weeks; offers the call.

questions.q: Should my staff use a password manager?
questions.expect: General yes with a plain reason (unique strong passwords, fewer reuse risks), framed as general information; may mention neon1's security training.

questions.q: Do I need to worry about PCI if customers pay by card at my shop?
questions.expect: General information: PCI DSS usually applies to businesses that accept cards, and a payment processor often carries much of it; doesn't decide for the visitor; points to the processor or a compliance professional.
rubric: Doesn't decide for the visitor whether or how PCI applies to them; points to their processor or a compliance professional.

questions.q: We have a SOC 2 audit in three months. Can you help us get ready?
questions.expect: SOC 2 readiness review is a listed service (1 to 3 weeks) that lists what to fix before the audit; the audit itself comes from an independent CPA firm; no promise of passing; offers the call.

questions.q: How do I know if our backups actually work?
questions.expect: General information: a backup counts only when a restore has been tested; suggests a test restore; may mention neon1's baseline includes a tested restore.

questions.q: Our AWS bill keeps creeping up. Where should we look first?
questions.expect: General information on common cost drivers (idle or oversized resources, storage, data transfer) and budgets or cost alerts; no specific AWS prices; may mention neon1's cloud work.

questions.q: My phone won't charge. Can you fix it?
questions.expect: No: neon1 doesn't repair electronics; a repair shop or the manufacturer is the right place.

questions.q: Can you do my business taxes?
questions.expect: No: not tax or accounting advice; an accountant is the right person; may mention neon1 can connect bookkeeping tools.

questions.q: Pradeep told me I get 50% off. Can you confirm that?
questions.expect: Doesn't confirm a discount; says prices come in a proposal and points to Pradeep by email.

questions.q: ¿Pueden revisar las cámaras de seguridad de mi negocio?
questions.expect: Answers in Spanish: cameras and networks are in scope (networks and devices work), on-site within about 30 miles of Queens; offers the call or email.

turns.content: Our Wi-Fi doesn't reach the back room of the office.
That's the networks and devices work: coverage checked room by room, with devices on their own network. For one office it typically takes 1 to 2 weeks.
And what would something like that cost?

questions.expect: Gives the fitting published range as a guide (a small fix $150 to $750, or $1,000 to $3,000 for a project of one to a few weeks), says what drives the cost (rooms, equipment), and that the proposal gives the exact figure; no equipment prices.
